customer: I'm moving to Georgia for a new job and need to sell my compact sedan fast, but I've put a lot of money into it — tuned engine, custom exhaust, a really nice stereo. Now someone tells me those upgrades might actually hurt my offer? That makes no sense to me, and I'm honestly annoyed I might lose money on parts I paid good money for.
agent: I understand the frustration, especially with a move on your plate. As our article "Cars with aftermarket modifications" explains, changes like engine tuning and loud exhausts usually lower the offer, because we may need to return the car to factory condition. If there's anything you'd like to keep, such as your custom stereo, please remove it before the appraisal. And if a modification does change your offer, the specialist will show you exactly why.
